directAnswer: Use Carbon Copy Cloner or SuperDuper to clone your Mac while logged in, ensuring FileVault is unlocked. After cloning, enable FileVault on the new SSD through System Settings.
summary: To clone a Mac to a new SSD without losing FileVault, use a cloning tool that supports APFS volumes while the system is unlocked. After cloning, re-enable FileVault on the new drive.

sections.heading: Internal vs. External SSD Options
sections.body: Most modern Macs, especially those with Apple silicon, have non-removable internal SSDs. For these, cloning to an external SSD is the practical option. Older Intel Macs may allow internal SSD replacements.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Cloning Software
sections.body: Carbon Copy Cloner and SuperDuper are recommended for cloning APFS volumes. They ensure the system is copied in a bootable state and handle the complexities of macOS's signed system volumes.

sections.heading: FileVault Considerations
sections.body: FileVault encrypts your data at rest. Cloning should be done while logged in to ensure the volume is decrypted. After cloning, FileVault must be re-enabled on the new SSD to maintain encryption.

steps.title: Prepare the New SSD
steps.detail: Connect the new SSD using a USB-C/Thunderbolt enclosure. Use Disk Utility to format it as APFS with a GUID partition map.

steps.title: Clone the Mac
steps.detail: Log in to your Mac to ensure FileVault is unlocked. Use Carbon Copy Cloner or SuperDuper to clone the system volume to the new SSD, following the software's instructions for a bootable copy.

steps.title: Test the Cloned SSD
steps.detail: Boot from the new SSD: on Apple silicon, hold the power button for startup options; on Intel, hold Option at boot. Verify that the system boots correctly and check FileVault status.

steps.title: Enable FileVault on the New SSD
steps.detail: Once the clone is verified, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → FileVault to enable encryption on the new SSD.

faqs.question: Will my FileVault recovery key transfer to the new SSD?
faqs.answer: No, you will need to generate a new recovery key when you enable FileVault on the new SSD.

faqs.question: Can I use Disk Utility to clone my Mac?
faqs.answer: Disk Utility can copy data, but for a bootable clone, use Carbon Copy Cloner or SuperDuper, which handle APFS and system volumes better.

faqs.question: What if my Mac has soldered storage?
faqs.answer: For Macs with soldered storage, use an external SSD for cloning and booting, as internal upgrades are not possible.

caveats: External booting on Apple silicon may depend on the enclosure and macOS version; test before erasing the internal drive.
Ensure the new SSD is compatible with your Mac's hardware and macOS version.
